learn.title: Grid Balancing Act: Keeping Lights On
learn.intro: Real-time electricity matching is vital for preventing blackouts as renewable energy grows. Without storage, grids struggle to balance wind/solar variability—balancing acts ensure reliability.
learn.c1_text: Power plants adjust output to match demand within seconds. Like a traffic controller managing cars, grid operators use automated systems to maintain stable frequency (50Hz in India), preventing cascading failures.
learn.c2_text: AI predicts solar/wind output using weather data. In India, grid forecasts reduce coal reliance by 15% (2023), enabling 35 GW of renewables to operate without curtailment.
learn.c3_text: India's grid manages 600 GW variable renewables by 2030. Current losses hit ₹45,000 crore annually, but smart grid investments aim to cut this by 30% by 2027.
learn.stat2: Grid response needs: 10 GW battery storage by 2028

learn.title: Wind Site Science: Finding Invisible Power
learn.intro: Wind resource assessment combines satellite data and ground sensors to identify optimal turbine locations. This science reduces project costs by 30% globally.
learn.c1_text: Instrument towers measure wind speed at turbine height (80-120m). In Gujarat, 10m/s average winds enable 2 GW Jamnagar wind farm efficiency.
learn.c2_text: Light detection and ranging maps wind patterns without turbines. India's National Institute of Wind Energy uses lidar at 30+ sites, reducing project risks by 40%.
learn.c3_text: Karnataka's Western Ghats wind corridor generates 8.5 GW. Tamil Nadu's 4,000+ turbines meet 12% of state demand, with 30% capacity factor.
learn.stat3: National wind mapping: ₹120 crore annual savings

learn.title: Green Steel Revolution: Hydrogen's Forge
learn.intro: Steel production accounts for 7% of global emissions. Hydrogen-based direct reduction replaces coal, cutting emissions by 90%—key for decarbonizing heavy industry.
learn.c1_text: Hydrogen reacts with iron ore at 800°C, producing pure molten iron. In Sweden, HYBRIT technology uses 90% green hydrogen, eliminating 1.8 tons CO2 per ton steel.
learn.c2_text: Traditional blast furnaces use 1.5 tons coal per ton steel. Hydrogen-based methods reduce energy use by 30% and enable 100% carbon capture potential.
learn.c3_text: Tata Steel's TATA ACE plant in Tamil Nadu uses hydrogen DRI, cutting emissions by 1.2 million tons annually. India aims for 10% green steel by 2030.
learn.stat3: India's steel sector: ₹1.5 lakh crore green investments (2024)
learn.stat4: National steel policy: 30% carbon intensity reduction by 2030

learn.title: Carbon Credits: Money for Clean Air
learn.intro: Carbon markets let polluters buy credits to offset emissions. India's CME platform trades 100,000+ contracts monthly, funding solar projects and forest restoration.
learn.c1_text: Governments set emission caps. India's 2022 carbon trading scheme allows power plants to buy credits at ₹150-250/ton, funding renewable upgrades.
learn.c2_text: Projects earn credits by reducing emissions. A Gujarat wind farm generates 5 lakh CERs/year, each worth ~$15, funding local healthcare.
learn.c3_text: India's carbon market size reached $2.3 billion in 2023. The PM Gati Shakti plan links railway electrification to carbon credits, targeting 200 MMtCO2 reduction by 2030.

learn.title: EV Mechanics: Motion and Energy
learn.intro: Electric vehicles convert battery power to motion with 90% efficiency. Regenerative braking recovers 15-25% energy, doubling range in city driving.
learn.c1_text: Permanent magnet motors convert 95% of electricity to motion. A Tata Tigor EV's 80 kW motor accelerates 0-60 km/h in 8 seconds using 18 kWh.
learn.c2_text: Braking converts kinetic energy to electricity. Indian EVs recover 1.2 kWh/100 km in cities, extending range by 25% compared to highway driving.
learn.c3_text: India has 3.5 million EVs (2024), with 60% two-wheelers. FAME II subsidies support 150,000 charging stations, targeting 50% EV penetration by 2030.

learn.title: PPAs: Powering Project Finance
learn.intro: Power Purchase Agreements lock in renewable energy prices for 15-25 years. In India, solar PPAs average ₹2.50/kWh, attracting $12 billion in investments since 2017.
learn.c1_text: Developers sell electricity at fixed rates. A Rajasthan solar farm secured a ₹2.44/kWh PPA in 2021, lower than grid tariffs, ensuring 10-year revenue certainty.
learn.c2_text: PPAs include volume guarantees. India's 2022 solar policy mandates 40% of procurement through PPAs, enabling 12 GW annual installations.
learn.c3_text: 2022-23 saw ₹45,000 crore PPA-backed projects. The 2024 National Electricity Policy proposes open access for 100% renewable PPAs, targeting 500 GW non-fossil capacity by 2030.
learn.stat4: Open access target: 100% renewable PPAs by 2030
